thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: p99 tail latency SLO breach detected for service=canary-inference eu-west1, rolling 5m p99=3.4s (SLO=2.0s). Alerts: streaming stalls increasing, user-facing errors up ~0.7%.
Mia L: acked. I'm the oncall. Starting triage — putting notes here.
Omar: grabbing metrics. Which model roll went to canary?
Samir: Canary got model v9.2 this morning at ~08:15UTC, traffic ramp to 15%. No infra changes.
Devin: I see p95 at 800ms but p99 spike to 3.4s, tail looks like token generation stalls during KV cache miss hotpath.
Irene: Streaming stall spikes visible in per-route dashboard: /v1/chat/stream shows increased frame gaps (200-400ms gaps) starting 08:40UTC.
Mia L: any customer reports? Alex (support) pls coordinate.
Alex (support): A couple of customers reported websockets disconnects and partial responses. CS notified 2 enterprise accounts; prepping status note.
Samir: dump of runtime logs for affected instances (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T08:41:03Z canary-node-7 shard=3 KV-lookup miss seq=256 latency=0.27s
2026-03-15T08:41:03Z canary-node-7 shard=3 fetch-remote-kv backend=kv-cluster-2 latency=2.1s
2026-03-15T08:41:04Z canary-node-7 stream-chunk delay=380ms tokens=64
```
Devin: That fetch-remote-kv 2.1s stands out. KV cluster eu-west1-b shows elevated p99 fetch latencies. Could be network or cache warming pattern from new model variant causing different key distribution.
Omar: Are we seeing increased cold starts or tokenization variance? Tokenizer p99 okay. It's the KV fetches.
Mia L: Run quick blast mitigation: reduce canary traffic from 15% -> 5% and pin traffic away from nodes in eu-west1-b. If that reduces p99, we can decide to rollback.
Samir: Applying partial traffic shift now. Running command:
```
# control-plane ops
redwoodctl traffic shift --service canary-inference --from v9.2 --to v9.1 --percent 10 --region eu-west1
```
Samir: Done. Verified control-plane accepted change. Rolling shift should complete in ~30s.
ProductOps Bot: Routing policy change: scaled 10% -> previous variant v9.1; changed weight: v9.1=85%, v9.2=15% -> v9.1=95%, v9.2=5%.
Devin: watching metrics...
Mia L: also enable KV-prefetch temporary config for v9.2 instances to reduce remote fetches while we investigate. Samir, can you toggle prefetch?
Samir: toggled prefetch=true for canary v9.2 nodes in eu-west1.
Irene: p99 trending down: 3.4s -> 1.9s within 60s after shift and prefetch. p95 stable ~700ms. Streaming frame gap metric reduced.
Alex (support): Notifying impacted customers: short note explaining degraded responses and that we reduced canary traffic and applied mitigations; offering postmortem if needed.
Mia L: Good. Continue to monitor for 15 minutes. If stable, we'll keep v9.2 at 5% and schedule rollback/rollforward decision.
Devin: Root cause hypothesis: v9.2 inference graph increases rare KV keys due to different attention window encoding; cold key distribution triggered remote fetch chain causing tail latency. Need to run offline trace to confirm.
Samir: I'll pull a sample of request traces (trace IDs) hitting remote KV during spike and map keys.
Omar: Also check network/multi-AZ routing — eu-west1-b tmux logs show occasional packet loss to kv-cluster-2 at 08:40. Correlates with fetch latency.
ProductOps Bot: Incident severity: SEV-2 (customer-facing but mitigated). Notifying oncall lead.
Mia L: tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for post-incident follow-up: document model-induced hotkey patterns & add test in canary harness.
Devin: Quick temporary play: enable serve-fallback to smaller context variant for streaming routes under >1s token delay. Applying now as experiment on 5% of traffic.
Samir: fallback applied on 5% traffic slice.
Irene: after fallback + prefetch + traffic shift p99=1.6s, errors down to baseline.
Alex (support): customers acknowledged the update; no escalations so far.
Mia L: Ready for handoff at 09:20UTC to follow-up rotation. Leaving this thread with summary and actions.
- Mitigation actions taken: reduced v9.2 weight 15%->5%, enabled KV prefetch on v9.2, applied serve-fallback on 5% slice.
- Observable improvement: p99 down from 3.4s -> 1.6s in ~3m.
- Next steps: eng-ml diagnose model key distribution; eng-runtime add circuit-breaker for slow KV; ops to investigate eu-west1-b network blips.
Mia L: handing off to Omar (follow-up oncall) — please take this and coordinate postmortem.
Omar: ack. I'll own follow-up. Creating follow-up doc and scheduling postmortem with teams. Closing active paging. :white_check_mark:
